title: CONSENSUS-FIT: how much of a model's standing in a reference-based arena is being RIGHT, and how much is AGREEING WITH THE FIELD? (zero calls)
question: Weighted logistic of the verdict on two signed contrasts (KEY, REF) fitted on ARENA-13 arm A (ensemble reference, n = 1,800) and x12 MAIN (the deployed grok reference, n = 9,142); plus a model-level fit of BT theta on standardised accuracy and standardised ensemble agreement, n = 13; falsifier stated in advance: if REF is not significantly positive once KEY is controlled, the consensus mechanism is unsupported.

plain_description.what: Statistical model fitted on existing judged matches (no new calls): how much does the judge's verdict depend on a model being actually correct versus agreeing with the reference answer the judge is shown?
plain_description.why: If an LLM judge mostly rewards agreement with its reference, an arena measures conformity, not correctness.
plain_description.information: A large agreement effect would show the arena rewards matching the reference. Result: done; agreeing with the reference weighs about 2.7 times as much as being right, but this is an upper bound (part of it appears even when no reference is shown). At the model level nothing can be separated (correctness and agreement are almost the same), so an earlier 'consensus' explanation of one model's lead was withdrawn. Note: this test is on the older p2dca question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
